chapter: New York 1936-39 (second pass of the transcript)
title: Arriving in New York and Serious Meyers (second pass)
summary: He stays with a drummer, carries his bass around and takes over Meyers's rehearsal with Billy Hicks.

bands.name: Billy Hicks and His Sizzling Six

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah. And I never went back to Philly.
What did you do, you just found an apartment, or a hotel?

No, I stayed with the drummer that had replaced the drummer, Sam Clark. I don't want to leave his name out, he's deceased. I stayed at his apartment and I made every rehearsal that was called upon. I was carrying my bass up and down 7th Avenue every day, you know, because I was from
Philly and a square, this is what we would have done in Philly.
You get to the rehearsal and it's supposed to be eight pieces and maybe six will show, you know, and so you got to call it off, so I went through that too.
Who did you meet in that period, who was around?
I met everybody. Which will bring me to Meyers. He didn't pay me in Philadelphia. He came and collected the money and came right back to New York.
After you had subbed for him?
Yeah, and he was one of the first persons I met when I came to New York. And he was rehearsing with Billy Hicks and his Sizzling Six, so he was too busy and he gave me the rehearsal.
Was that kind of a way of paying you back.
